$comment: Regression eval cases for dream-memory recall. Each case defines a query and the expected outcome (target, category, content match). Used by /dream-eval to measure precision@k and recall@k against the current scoring heuristics (BM25 + score floor + decay + IDF anchor). Adding a new case = documenting a new invariant.

cases.description: Recall a pt-BR preference about the user's editor. Tests diacritic handling and target filtering.
Recall a convention about terminal config from project memory.
Surface a known tool-quirk/failure pattern for a specific tool.
Recall a correction the user gave (replaces a previous instruction).
Find a permanent factual memory (e.g., a phone number or system fact).
Recall a derived insight (query-synthesis) — should rank highly because of higher tier.
Recall a project-specific convention (not bleeding to global).
Recall an agent-scoped convention (only visible to that agent).
Test that the recall system surfaces a memory even when query has negation words.
Query in en, memory content in pt-BR — tests cross-language recall.
A specific factual detail (UUID-like). Anchor token should match.
Recent memory (not yet decay-weighted heavily) should rank high.
Verify that project-scope query does NOT leak global-scope memories. Negative test.
Surface a failure memory by searching for the error pattern it describes.
A factual memory with rare tokens. Tests IDF anchor selection.

Search for an English negative preference. Verifies search handles 'not'/'don't' tokens correctly. The contradiction detection (in detectContradictions) checks hasNegationMismatch to force keep-both for opposite-polarity pairs — this case documents the search side, the integration test in evals/integration.test.ts covers the action side.
Search for a pt-BR negative preference. The 'não' token is critical for contradiction detection — pair with 'uso Zed' (positive) it triggers negation mismatch → keep-both.
Both memories have negation. Should NOT trigger negation mismatch (both are negative). Bigram similarity still applies.
Sanity check: similar positive memories. No negation involved, regular contradiction flow applies. Ensures the negation fix doesn't regress normal case detection.
Add two related memories and verify the second one has the first in its linked_to list. Auto-link should kick in for content with shared key terms.
Search for a query that matches a memory's content, verify the linked memory appears in results via expansion. Tests the 1-hop graph traversal in scopedSearch.
Sanity check: a memory doesn't link to itself. The excludeId param in findRelatedMemories should prevent this.
Different target types don't link. A user preference shouldn't auto-link with a project convention, even if content overlaps.
F10: Query about a topic that doesn't exist in the corpus. System should abstain (return low scores).
F10: Gibberish query with no semantic overlap. System should return nothing meaningful.
F10: Query for a specific UUID that doesn't exist. Should not match any memory.
F10: Query about a technology/domain not in the corpus. Should abstain.
